name: GTD Clarification and the Two-Minute Rule
diagnostic: Ambiguity-induced task postponement. Ambiguously defined tasks require high activation energy to parse, while trivial items generate administrative backlog disproportionate to their actual execution cost.

procedure.text: Take the top item in the inbox and judge it alone, without scanning the items beneath it.
Decide whether it is actionable. If not, trash it, file it as reference, or park it on an incubation list.
If it is actionable, name the one physical next action that moves it forward.
If that action takes 120 seconds or less, do it now and close the record.
If it takes longer, delegate it or put it on a project backlog or a context list.

trap: Using the two-minute rule as a habit: running micro-tasks back to back for hours. Deep work derails and you become a purely reactive machine.
procedureFull:
1. Isolate the topmost raw item in the capture inbox; evaluate it independently without scanning subsequent items.
2. Determine if the item is actionable. If not: trash it, archive it as reference, or file it under a deferred incubation list.
3. If actionable, specify the physical, unambiguous next action required for forward progress.
4. Determine execution duration: if completion requires ≤ 120 seconds, execute immediately and terminate the record.
5. If the action requires > 120 seconds, delegate the item or append it to a project backlog or contextual execution list.
setupFull: Raw Input: "Docker container crashes on boot" Clarified Next Action: "Run docker logs --tail 50 app_server to extract panic trace" Execution Estimate: 30 seconds -> [Executed immediately; record marked complete]
trapFull: Utilizing the two-minute window to execute micro-tasks sequentially for hours. This causes deep-work derailment and transforms the user into a purely reactive state machine.
